docs.text: Driver BNO08x Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the CEVA BNO080, BNO085 and BNO086 smart sensor hubs. It speaks SHTP and SH-2 over I2C, SPI and UART, and the stand-alone UART-RVC mode, on any MCU, with no heap and no blocking call. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves bytes on your bus and reads a pin or two; it does the rest: the start-up handshake, SHTP framing and its checks, the SH-2 reports and commands, timestamps, calibration, tare and the configuration records. Smart sensor hub BNO080, BNO085, BNO086 CEVA Function Accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer fused by the MotionEngine into rotation vectors, motion and activity reports Interface I2C (0x4A or 0x4B), SPI mode 3 up to 3 MHz, UART-SHTP at 3 Mbit/s, or UART-RVC at 115200 baud; chosen by two strap pins at reset Reports Every sensor report of the SH-2 reference manual, batched and timestamped, from 1 Hz to 1 kHz Configuration Calibration, tare, orientation and the flash record store (FRS), read and written by record Supply VDD 2.4 V to 3.6 V, VDDIO 1.7 V to 3.6 V What you get ¶ One object, four transports. Bno08x<YourPort> takes a port that names its transport; the I2C, SPI, UART-SHTP and UART-RVC paths share the same API. See Transports . Never blocks. Begin() starts a session and Poll() does all the work in small steps. Operations return an OpId and finish with an event. See Architecture . Every sensor report decoded. One event type with the report's values in its own units, a timestamp and the accuracy. See Sensors . Calibration, tare and FRS. Typed calls for every command of the manual, and generic record read and write. See Calibration . Strict where the documents are, tolerant where they are not. Every place the documents disagree or are silent is a named ambiguity with a configuration knob. See Ambiguities . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. Buffers are template parameters. See Contract . Tested without hardware. Host tests run the driver against an independent model of the hub on all four transports, and a fuzzer corrupts what the hub sends. See Testing and CI . docs.text: Agent context ¶ What an agent needs before it touches this repository: the flow, the skill for each step, the exact local checks, the file layout, the standing rules, the pitfalls that failed CI before, and when to stop. Read AGENTS.md for the repository itself. This page is managed by the template ( scaffold.py --check-drift --fix ships it) and tools/check_skills.py checks that every skill named here exists and that the files its commands name exist. 1. The flow and the skill for each step ¶ Each step has an input, an output and an exit rule. Do not skip a step and do not start the next before the exit rule holds. # Step Skill Output Exit rule 0 Plan: new driver, extension or duplicate, and the API shape plan-driver placement.md with a verdict Verdict NEW ; otherwise stop or extend 1 Scaffold new-driver-from-template A building driver with the example chip renamed verify passes on the untouched scaffold 2 Build from the datasheet datasheet-conformance , add-driver-feature , add-port Register map, model, tests, driver, port, examples, docs Host tests green; every datasheet topic recorded 3 Self-review cpp20-profile , misra-review , hardware-lessons-review Findings fixed Every catalogue class in recurring-defects.md answered 4 Verify verify Local gate result tools/preflight.sh ends 0 failure(s) 5 Independent review review-round A report per round NO BLOCKER and no MAJOR 6 First-push gate first-push Container rehearsal and the evidence list 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) 7 Publish publish-driver Public repository, one commit, green main , Pages CI gate / gate green on main ; the owner did the owner-only steps 8 Release candidate release Tag v0.1.0-rc.N Release workflow green; checksums verified 9 Hardware hardware-validation Level H0, H1 or H2 stated and evidenced Badge, driver.yml and release text agree 10 After release bump-pin A pin-bump pull request per consumer Consumer CI green A change to an existing driver skips steps 0, 1 and 7: use add-driver-feature or add-port , then steps 3 to 5 and a pull request (AGENTS.md, "Branches, commits and pull requests"). The agent safety-reviewer runs the review skills read-only. 2. The local gate: commands and what passes ¶ Run from the repository root. Set VENV (a venv with the docs theme, lizard, yamllint), CI_TOOLS_DIR (a kokeb-labs/ci-tools checkout) and CLANG_TIDY (version 20) when the tools are not on PATH . A step the preflight skips is named in its last line: install the tool; do not push around it. Command Passes when tools/preflight.sh Last line == 0 failure(s) and no skip you can fix tools/preflight.sh --container 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) (coverage, ASan/UBSan, fuzz in the CI image) python3 tools/scaffold.py --check-drift . no template drift (or each difference is listed under local with a reason) python3 tools/check_standalone.py Exit 0: no other project's name, no dated history, the right copyright holder python3 -I tools/check_skills.py Every skill named in this page exists, has front matter, and names existing files python3 -I tools/check_layout.py One source per header, SDK code only in src/boundary/ python3 -I tools/check_hardware.py driver.yml hardware level, README badge and rig document agree python3 -I tools/check_language.py driver.yml language: block and every place that repeats the C++ standard agree ( --fix rewrites them) python3 tools/misra_lint.py --root . No error; fix warnings in files you touch kokeb-docs figures && kokeb-docs gen && kokeb-docs check No diff afterwards ( git diff --exit-code docs README.md ) mkdocs build -f _config/mkdocs.yml --strict -d /tmp/site Exit 0, no warning git ls-files | grep -i '\.pdf$' No output git add -A && git ls-files -s examples/esp32/scripts Mode 160000 (a gitlink), if examples/esp32 exists CI-only checks, which a workstation cannot run: the MISRA scan and the ESP32 builds. Cover them by reading the misra-review skill and building examples/esp32 with the ESP-IDF version in examples/esp32/app_config.yml (the scripts are in examples/esp32/scripts , Platforms ) when ESP-IDF is installed. Delete the build directories afterwards; never run docker system prune or any other prune on a shared machine. Run one container job at a time and cmake --build ... --parallel 3 at most when other agents are working. 3. File layout ¶ One source per header, same stem. inc/<stem>.hpp has src/<stem>.cpp (or .ipp for a header-only template driver). A header that declares only constants, types, details, registers, the Kconfig defaults or the port contract ( _types , _detail , _registers , _kconfig , _interface ) needs no source. A header with real logic always has its own source. A header that holds only templates, constants or inline types may instead be listed under header_only in tools/layout.yml with a one-line reason (no colon followed by a space in it); nothing else is exempt. No combined file ( a_and_b.cpp ): split it by header. SDK-touching code (ESP-IDF, an RTOS, a vendor HAL) is never in inc/ or in src/ 's logic: it lives one file per SDK component in src/boundary/<component>.cpp , named after the component, so the directory carries the layering rule. A driver normally has none: it reaches hardware only through the port hooks, and the SDK appears only in examples/<platform>/ . The only generated SDK header read by the driver is sdkconfig.h , in inc/<name>_kconfig.hpp . examples/<platform>/ is the only platform code; examples/host/ always exists. Tests do not include SDK headers. Tool configuration is in _config/ only: no copies or symlinks at the root. The root holds only the files AGENTS.md lists. Never commit build*/ , a venv, a PDF, logs or a scratch file. tools/layout.yml (optional) lists the exceptions: header_only , internal , boundary_extra , each with a reason that tools/check_layout.py also keeps current. 4. Naming ¶ Namespace and package are the part number in lower case; files <name>.hpp , <name>_<topic>.hpp ; public methods PascalCase, private camelBack, members snake_case_ , constants kPascalCase , units as suffixes ( TimeoutMs , VoltageMv ); include guards <NAME>_<FILE_STEM>_<EXT> ; enumerations enum class with EnumLast , never a sentinel value; chip-specific Error values from 16. The repository is driver-<part> ; the copyright holder is The driver-<part> authors . Full rules: AGENTS.md and the handbook. 5. Docs and diagrams ¶ Every claim about the chip cites a datasheet section and page; docs/datasheets.yml records vendor, number, revision, date, URL, SHA-256 and one topic per section used. The PDF itself is never committed. docs/hardware.yml is the one description of the chip (package, pins, supply, hooks, blocks, a circuit, the README's overview, capabilities and frames). The pinout, outline, block diagram, wiring and frame figures, the chip card and the coverage table are generated from it and the headers: never draw or type them by hand. The README and docs/index.md lead with the chip (summary, hero figure, capabilities, uses, inside the chip, pins and wiring), then the quick start and the driver coverage; the layering figure is on the architecture page only. Code shown on the site lives in tests/docs/ between --8<-- markers and is compiled. Every public symbol has a Doxygen comment. CHANGELOG.md has ## [Unreleased] with the allowed headings only. A claim of behaviour in docs, comments or the build report names the code and the test that back it (RD-09). Anything only a bench can confirm is marked not verified on hardware with bench steps, and the level is stated ( hardware-validation skill). 6. Standing rules ¶ Stand-alone. The repository describes its own part and nothing else: no product, board, project, person or other repository by name, no lab history, no dates outside release headings, datasheet revisions and waiver expiries. Behaviour learned on a bench is written as the design with its datasheet section. Copyright is The <repo> authors in LICENSE , every source header, driver.yml and the docs footer. Do not put a company or a person there. No attribution. No Co-Authored-By: trailers, "Generated with" footers or tool names in commits, pull requests or files. Commits are signed off ( git commit -s ) with the owner's GitHub noreply address; no personal email address appears anywhere, and security reports go through GitHub advisories ( .github/SECURITY.md ). No secrets (tokens, keys, credentials, personal addresses) and no vendor PDFs or other licensed documents anywhere in the tree, the history, a pull request or a log you attach. Datasheets are fetched only from the vendor's public page into a scratch folder; never bypass a login or a 403, never fetch the same blocked URL again; record the gap and stop that item. Owner-only actions: making a repository public, rulesets and security settings, deleting or recreating a repository, force-pushing, the final release tag. publish-driver lists them. Ask; do not assume. No force-push to main and no history rewrite of a published branch. Never move or delete a tag. Open source references are read for ideas about API shape; no code, table or text is copied from a source whose licence you have not recorded, and none from an unlicensed or copyleft one. Conserve CI. Push only when the local gate passed; push the fixes together; re-run only infrastructure failures ( release skill, section 5). The datasheet is the source of behaviour. When it is silent or contradicts another source, write the design decision and its reason, make the model knob switchable, and list the bench step. Do not change the model to match a bench result without reading the datasheet again. 7. Known pitfalls and the fix ¶ Pitfall Fix The C++ lint job hits its 20-minute limit when the test sources are in the compilation database twice (the unit tests and their optimised copy) or the clang-analyzer runs over every test The preflight times its tidy step and fails over 400 s (a third of the limit). Fix: put the optimised copy ( <name>_optimised_build ) behind a CMake option that the lint workflow turns off, disable clang-analyzer-* for tests/ in tests/.clang-tidy (the analyzer still covers the driver through examples/host ), and keep the suite in few, small translation units The MISRA scan builds with an unbounded make -j and loses the runner on a large tree Give the scan its own small target (headers alone, snippets, examples, fuzz) and bound the job count ( CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=2 ) Local clang-tidy, clang-format or CMake differ from CI Use clang-tidy 20 and clang-format 20 ( CLANG_TIDY , CLANG_FORMAT ); other versions report different findings and a green local run proves nothing ESP-IDF differs between versions (v5.5 is pinned; v6 changes peripheral drivers and error codes, for example an SPI polling transfer accepts only an infinite wait, a bus NACK maps to another error code) Build examples/esp32 with the version in app_config.yml ; use only APIs present in it; do not add an IDF version column without the owner; list every REQUIRES component the example includes MISRA findings on vendor enumerations, esp_err_t values and C naming from an SDK Keep SDK types out of the driver; convert at the edge in src/boundary/<component>.cpp ; use enum class and fixed-width types in the public API A stale deviation marker (a MISRA deviation comment, or a tools/layout.yml / waiver entry) outlives the code it excused Remove the marker in the same commit as the code; the checks fail on an entry that names nothing _u8 / _u16 / _u32 literal operators raise rule 6.9.2 (they take unsigned long long ) Follow the misra-review skill's current pattern for typed constants; do not add new literal operators; ask when unsure An unused named parameter (rule 0.2.2), a discarded std::copy result (0.1.2), char arithmetic (7.0.3), differing parameter names (13.3.3), an else -less chain (9.4.1) Unnamed parameter or static_cast<void> ; static_cast<void>(std::copy(...)) ; compare characters with std::char_traits ; same names in header and definition; final else . tools/misra_lint.py finds most Indirect recursion (8.2.10) between small helpers Draw the call graph of retry and recovery paths; make one function the only caller of the other .gitignore drops a file the build needs ( *.bin silently removes fuzz corpus inputs) Check what git will push, not the working tree: git status --ignored , and git add -A && git ls-files tests/fuzz The host-example CI step runs ./build-example-<cc>/<name>_host_example ; a driver with other example binary names exits 127 after all tests pass Keep the single example target name, or change the workflow input and the preflight together Host builds on macOS cannot see type-width bugs ( %d with int32_t , PRId64 under strict C++20 on newlib, int main(int32_t, ...) ) Compile the sources for a newlib target ( -fsyntax-only ); cast to long long for %lld ; use uint32_t and main(int, char**) Unspecified evaluation order in a check (GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left) Compute the driver result into a local before reading the state it changes (RD-34); tools/eval_order_check.py A clock comparison with half-range logic stops working after 2^31 ms Use unsigned elapsed subtraction ( now - start >= limit ); fuzz with the clock near wrap Container build killed by out-of-memory ( Killed signal terminated program cc1plus ) Pass CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=4 or lower to the container; never run two container jobs at once macOS libFuzzer hangs in symbolization and leaves processes behind Set ASAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=0 UBSAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=0 and -print_funcs=0 ; kill orphans afterwards scaffold.py --check-drift fails on .kokeb/template.yml Keep each value on one line; a long description may continue with a trailing \ . Never hand-edit template: A tag was pushed to the wrong commit Do not move or delete it (a ruleset forbids it); cut the next -rc.N and say why Docs figures or generated regions differ between machines Run kokeb-docs figures && kokeb-docs gen with the pinned theme version, commit the result, never edit generated regions 8. When to stop and report instead of improvising ¶ Stop, write down what you saw, what you tried and what you need, and hand it back when: the placement verdict is not NEW , or plan-driver ends BLOCKED ; the datasheet cannot be obtained without a login, a bypassed 403 or a licence you cannot confirm, or two datasheet revisions disagree on something the driver depends on; a check fails twice for the same reason and you do not understand the cause, or a CI failure is outside the repository (a shared workflow, a runner, the quota) and is not an infrastructure failure the release skill lists; a fix needs a waiver, a change to a managed file (anything --check-drift ships), a new ESP-IDF version, or a change to kokeb-labs/ci-tools , the handbook or the shared catalogue; an action is owner-only (section 6), irreversible, or touches anything outside this repository; a safety question arises (the chip can switch a load, heat, move or hold a high voltage) that the datasheet does not answer, or a bench result contradicts the datasheet; you find a secret, a vendor PDF, a person's or another project's name already in the tree or the history. An honest "not verified" in the report is worth more than a green check obtained by weakening a test, a lint or a rule. Never do that.

docs.title: 3. File layout

docs.text: Namespace and package are the part number in lower case; files <name>.hpp , <name>_<topic>.hpp ; public methods PascalCase, private camelBack, members snake_case_ , constants kPascalCase , units as suffixes ( TimeoutMs , VoltageMv ); include guards <NAME>_<FILE_STEM>_<EXT> ; enumerations enum class with EnumLast , never a sentinel value; chip-specific Error values from 16. The repository is driver-<part> ; the copyright holder is The driver-<part> authors . Full rules: AGENTS.md and the handbook.
docs.title: 4. Naming

docs.text: Every claim about the chip cites a datasheet section and page; docs/datasheets.yml records vendor, number, revision, date, URL, SHA-256 and one topic per section used. The PDF itself is never committed. docs/hardware.yml is the one description of the chip (package, pins, supply, hooks, blocks, a circuit, the README's overview, capabilities and frames). The pinout, outline, block diagram, wiring and frame figures, the chip card and the coverage table are generated from it and the headers: never draw or type them by hand. The README and docs/index.md lead with the chip (summary, hero figure, capabilities, uses, inside the chip, pins and wiring), then the quick start and the driver coverage; the layering figure is on the architecture page only. Code shown on the site lives in tests/docs/ between --8<-- markers and is compiled. Every public symbol has a Doxygen comment. CHANGELOG.md has ## [Unreleased] with the allowed headings only. A claim of behaviour in docs, comments or the build report names the code and the test that back it (RD-09). Anything only a bench can confirm is marked not verified on hardware with bench steps, and the level is stated ( hardware-validation skill).
docs.title: 5. Docs and diagrams

docs.text: Stand-alone. The repository describes its own part and nothing else: no product, board, project, person or other repository by name, no lab history, no dates outside release headings, datasheet revisions and waiver expiries. Behaviour learned on a bench is written as the design with its datasheet section. Copyright is The <repo> authors in LICENSE , every source header, driver.yml and the docs footer. Do not put a company or a person there. No attribution. No Co-Authored-By: trailers, "Generated with" footers or tool names in commits, pull requests or files. Commits are signed off ( git commit -s ) with the owner's GitHub noreply address; no personal email address appears anywhere, and security reports go through GitHub advisories ( .github/SECURITY.md ). No secrets (tokens, keys, credentials, personal addresses) and no vendor PDFs or other licensed documents anywhere in the tree, the history, a pull request or a log you attach. Datasheets are fetched only from the vendor's public page into a scratch folder; never bypass a login or a 403, never fetch the same blocked URL again; record the gap and stop that item. Owner-only actions: making a repository public, rulesets and security settings, deleting or recreating a repository, force-pushing, the final release tag. publish-driver lists them. Ask; do not assume. No force-push to main and no history rewrite of a published branch. Never move or delete a tag. Open source references are read for ideas about API shape; no code, table or text is copied from a source whose licence you have not recorded, and none from an unlicensed or copyleft one. Conserve CI. Push only when the local gate passed; push the fixes together; re-run only infrastructure failures ( release skill, section 5). The datasheet is the source of behaviour. When it is silent or contradicts another source, write the design decision and its reason, make the model knob switchable, and list the bench step. Do not change the model to match a bench result without reading the datasheet again.
docs.title: 6. Standing rules

docs.text: Pitfall Fix The C++ lint job hits its 20-minute limit when the test sources are in the compilation database twice (the unit tests and their optimised copy) or the clang-analyzer runs over every test The preflight times its tidy step and fails over 400 s (a third of the limit). Fix: put the optimised copy ( <name>_optimised_build ) behind a CMake option that the lint workflow turns off, disable clang-analyzer-* for tests/ in tests/.clang-tidy (the analyzer still covers the driver through examples/host ), and keep the suite in few, small translation units The MISRA scan builds with an unbounded make -j and loses the runner on a large tree Give the scan its own small target (headers alone, snippets, examples, fuzz) and bound the job count ( CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=2 ) Local clang-tidy, clang-format or CMake differ from CI Use clang-tidy 20 and clang-format 20 ( CLANG_TIDY , CLANG_FORMAT ); other versions report different findings and a green local run proves nothing ESP-IDF differs between versions (v5.5 is pinned; v6 changes peripheral drivers and error codes, for example an SPI polling transfer accepts only an infinite wait, a bus NACK maps to another error code) Build examples/esp32 with the version in app_config.yml ; use only APIs present in it; do not add an IDF version column without the owner; list every REQUIRES component the example includes MISRA findings on vendor enumerations, esp_err_t values and C naming from an SDK Keep SDK types out of the driver; convert at the edge in src/boundary/<component>.cpp ; use enum class and fixed-width types in the public API A stale deviation marker (a MISRA deviation comment, or a tools/layout.yml / waiver entry) outlives the code it excused Remove the marker in the same commit as the code; the checks fail on an entry that names nothing _u8 / _u16 / _u32 literal operators raise rule 6.9.2 (they take unsigned long long ) Follow the misra-review skill's current pattern for typed constants; do not add new literal operators; ask when unsure An unused named parameter (rule 0.2.2), a discarded std::copy result (0.1.2), char arithmetic (7.0.3), differing parameter names (13.3.3), an else -less chain (9.4.1) Unnamed parameter or static_cast<void> ; static_cast<void>(std::copy(...)) ; compare characters with std::char_traits ; same names in header and definition; final else . tools/misra_lint.py finds most Indirect recursion (8.2.10) between small helpers Draw the call graph of retry and recovery paths; make one function the only caller of the other .gitignore drops a file the build needs ( *.bin silently removes fuzz corpus inputs) Check what git will push, not the working tree: git status --ignored , and git add -A && git ls-files tests/fuzz The host-example CI step runs ./build-example-<cc>/<name>_host_example ; a driver with other example binary names exits 127 after all tests pass Keep the single example target name, or change the workflow input and the preflight together Host builds on macOS cannot see type-width bugs ( %d with int32_t , PRId64 under strict C++20 on newlib, int main(int32_t, ...) ) Compile the sources for a newlib target ( -fsyntax-only ); cast to long long for %lld ; use uint32_t and main(int, char**) Unspecified evaluation order in a check (GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left) Compute the driver result into a local before reading the state it changes (RD-34); tools/eval_order_check.py A clock comparison with half-range logic stops working after 2^31 ms Use unsigned elapsed subtraction ( now - start >= limit ); fuzz with the clock near wrap Container build killed by out-of-memory ( Killed signal terminated program cc1plus ) Pass CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=4 or lower to the container; never run two container jobs at once macOS libFuzzer hangs in symbolization and leaves processes behind Set ASAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=0 UBSAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=0 and -print_funcs=0 ; kill orphans afterwards scaffold.py --check-drift fails on .kokeb/template.yml Keep each value on one line; a long description may continue with a trailing \ . Never hand-edit template: A tag was pushed to the wrong commit Do not move or delete it (a ruleset forbids it); cut the next -rc.N and say why Docs figures or generated regions differ between machines Run kokeb-docs figures && kokeb-docs gen with the pinned theme version, commit the result, never edit generated regions
docs.title: 7. Known pitfalls and the fix

docs.text: Stop, write down what you saw, what you tried and what you need, and hand it back when: the placement verdict is not NEW , or plan-driver ends BLOCKED ; the datasheet cannot be obtained without a login, a bypassed 403 or a licence you cannot confirm, or two datasheet revisions disagree on something the driver depends on; a check fails twice for the same reason and you do not understand the cause, or a CI failure is outside the repository (a shared workflow, a runner, the quota) and is not an infrastructure failure the release skill lists; a fix needs a waiver, a change to a managed file (anything --check-drift ships), a new ESP-IDF version, or a change to kokeb-labs/ci-tools , the handbook or the shared catalogue; an action is owner-only (section 6), irreversible, or touches anything outside this repository; a safety question arises (the chip can switch a load, heat, move or hold a high voltage) that the datasheet does not answer, or a bench result contradicts the datasheet; you find a secret, a vendor PDF, a person's or another project's name already in the tree or the history. An honest "not verified" in the report is worth more than a green check obtained by weakening a test, a lint or a rule. Never do that.
docs.title: 8. When to stop and report instead of improvising

docs.text: Ambiguities and decisions ¶ The CEVA documents disagree with each other in places, are silent in others, and describe chips that differ in small ways. This page lists every case the driver had to decide, what it decided, and the switch that changes it. Nothing here is verified on hardware: the driver is tested against an independent model of the hub whose Knobs reproduce each reading ( Testing and CI ), so a hub that behaves differently is a bench result to report, not a surprise in the field. Datasheet sections this page relies on Features, variants and what differs: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, Features (front page), p. 1 Motion, orientation and environmental outputs: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 2 Sensor data processing, p. 30 Interactive calibration (BNO086 only): CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 3.3 Interactive Calibration (BNO086 only), p. 39 Version history: BNO080 removed, polling note: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 8 Version history, p. 56 UART inputs of the RVC mode: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 3.1.2 UART Inputs, p. 12 Pin and interface differences from the BNO070: CEVA (Hillcrest Labs) none printed 1.6, 2.1 Pinout Comparisons, p. 7 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . 0 : 1 ) the API is a bool; model verifies both polarities A36 TARE cites RM S6.4.4.1 and S6.4.4.2 for tare now and persist; RM 1.9 numbers them S6.4.3.1, S6.4.3.2 RM 1.9 numbers used A37 Tare Now supports axes 0x07 and 0x04 (RM S6.4.3.1 prose) although P1 is a bitmap allowed masks 0x07 and 0x04; other masks InvalidArgument (knob tare_any_mask in the model) A38 DS p18: H_INTN should be handled within 1/10 of the fastest sensor period; hub times out after about 10 ms Poll guidance in docs; model hint_host_timeout_ms retries H_INTN A39 DS 1.2.2.1 says I2C "up to 400 kb/s"; the SPI limit is 3 MHz; UART 3 Mbit/s; no minimum host SPI clock is given constants only A40 CEVA's tare guide is titled for BNO085/BNO086; the calibration guide 1.3 for BNO080/BNO085 recorded, no behaviour A41 Pickup detector 0x1B: RM Figure 107 (p79) shows 6 bytes, the vendor library's length table 8 built-in length 6; an advertised ReportLengths entry wins; model pickup_report_len , advertise_report_lengths A42 Wheel encoder 0x2E: the RM has no report layout, the vendor library's length table says 12 no layout, SetFeature returns Unsupported ; with an advertised length a report is skipped and counted in unknown_report , without one the rest of its cargo is skipped; model wheel_encoder_len Not exposed: command 0x10 (dead-reckoning calibration save, sh2_saveDeadReckoningCalNow in the vendor library) is not in the RM command list (Figure 42, p44 and p45, IDs 1 to 14, plus 0x0F in S6.4.13), so the driver does not send it. Corrections found while checking the references ¶ Thirty-odd page and section references were compared with the PDFs when the driver was written. These are the ones that were wrong or imprecise in the working notes; the driver and docs/datasheets.yml use the corrected values. Reference as first noted Corrected Reports 0x13 and 0x1F are 5 bytes long 6 bytes (RM report-length table) One metadata record ID "0xE300" for all sensors One per sensor, 0xE301 to 0xE325; 0x2C and 0x2D have none 36 sensor input report IDs 39 (40 counting the reserved 0x17) DS p40, DS p18 DS p41, DS p19 RM section 6.5.2 p34, section 6.5 p42, Figure 75 p41 RM p63, p62, p62 to 63 RM section 7 p11, section 6.4.12.1 p12, Figure 111 p70 RM p91, p60, p81 to 82 SHTP Figure 16 p11, Figure 17 p12 SHTP p15, p17 DS section 1.4 p2 DS p1 to p2 One page offset for all documents PDF page = printed page + 1 for RM, SHTP, the SH-2 update guide and the calibration guides 1.3 and later; 0 for the data sheet, the tare guide and the migration guide "Accuracy under 10 degrees" from the data sheet The tare guide, page 2 Pin 1 marker described as the package feature The marker belongs to the land pattern drawing The tare and calibration guides carry typos the driver does not copy: the update guide's command byte 0xF2 where 0xFC is meant, and a tag number 8 where 9 is meant. The driver's sensor-to-report-ID table is internal; it is checked against the manual's figures, not against a library. Accuracy of the Euler helper ¶ ToEulerCentiDeg() converts a Q14 quaternion with integer arithmetic only. It is accurate to a few centidegrees in general; very close to a pitch of plus or minus 90 degrees yaw and roll are ill-defined and the error reaches about 80 centidegrees (the tests bound it there). Use the quaternion itself for control and Euler angles for display. Open questions for the vendor ¶ A2 (I2C polling by variant), A3 (BNO086 features), A6 (the RVC checksum range), A8 (the RVC inputs), A12 (the advertised limits), A14 (continuation reads), A15 (sequence numbers after reset), A17 (timestamp overflow), A27 (the FRS completion status), and whether any chip implements the manual-only sensors. Firmware update (the DFU protocol is not public, DS p29) is not supported.

docs.text: ToEulerCentiDeg() converts a Q14 quaternion with integer arithmetic only. It is accurate to a few centidegrees in general; very close to a pitch of plus or minus 90 degrees yaw and roll are ill-defined and the error reaches about 80 centidegrees (the tests bound it there). Use the quaternion itself for control and Euler angles for display.

API guide ¶ The driver's API by task, with code that compiles: start a session, run it, enable sensors, read events, handle errors, and use the operations. Datasheet sections this page relies on Report structure, product ID, executable commands: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.3.2 Report Structure, p. 23 Configuration and the commands list: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.3.3 BNO08X Configuration, p. 24 Feature reports, rate and batch: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 5.4 Feature Reports, p. 34 Product ID request and response: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.3.1 Product ID Request (0xF9), p. 39 Command request and response: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.3.8 Command Request (0xF2), p. 43 Report errors, counters, initialise: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.4.1 Report Errors (0x01), p. 45 Simple calibration, interactive calibration, wheel: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.4.10 Simple Calibration Commands (0x0C), p. 55 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The shape of the API ¶ Group Calls Session Begin() , Poll() , GetState() , Ready() , HardReset() , Reset() , HubOn() , HubSleep() Sensors SetFeature() , GetFeature() , Feature() , Flush() , ReadMetadata() , GetMetadata() Events PopEvent() , Latest() , AgeUs() , GetStats() Identification ReadProductId() , Product() , Advertised() , bno08x::GetDriverVersion() Calibration and orientation ConfigureMeCal() , GetMeCal() , SaveDcd() , SetPeriodicDcd() , ClearDcdAndReset() , Tare() , PersistTare() , SetReorientation() , ClearReorientation() , StartSimpleCal() , FinishSimpleCal() , SetMotionIntent() Records ReadFrs() , WriteFrs() , EraseFrs() Diagnostics GetOscillator() , Initialize() , GetCounts() , ClearCounts() , ReportErrors() , SendWheel() UART-RVC RvcSend() (guarded) A call that needs the hub returns Result<OpId> : check ok() and keep the id, or read error . The outcome arrives later as an OpDone event carrying that id. Result is [[nodiscard]] , so an unchecked call is a compiler warning. Calls that only look at what the driver already holds ( Feature() , Latest() , GetMetadata() , Product() ) return at once. Start a session ¶ bno08x :: Error BringUp ( Hub & hub , const bno08x :: Config & cfg ) { // Starts the session and returns at once. Poll() then runs the reset, the advertisement and the // initialise handshake; hub.Ready() turns true when it is done, and hub.GetState() says where it // is. const auto r = hub . Begin ( cfg ); if ( ! r . ok ()) { std :: printf ( "BNO08x begin: %s 
 " , bno08x :: ToString ( r . error )); } return r . error ; } Begin() validates the configuration, brings the port up and starts the reset; it does not wait. Call Poll() from your loop with a microsecond time (the same clock as the port's NowUs() ): it runs the reset wait, reads the advertisement and completes the initialise handshake, and Ready() turns true. GetState() says where it is; a step that exceeds startup_timeout_ms leaves the session Faulted , and Begin() (or HardReset() ) starts it again; a stop request (sensor off, Reset() , HubSleep() ) is still written while it is Faulted . The Quickstart has the whole loop. How often to call Poll() : at least once per tenth of the fastest report period. The hub gives up on a host that answers H_INTN much later (A38), and a slow Poll() adds to every sample's latency. Enable sensors and read events ¶ bno08x :: Error EnableBatched ( Hub & hub ) { bno08x :: FeatureConfig fc {}; fc . interval_us = 10000 ; // 100 Hz fc . batch_us = 100000 ; // deliver in groups every 100 ms return hub . SetFeature ( bno08x :: SensorId :: GyroscopeCalibrated , fc ). error ; } void Drain ( Hub & hub , bno08x :: OpId waiting_for ) { bno08x :: Event e {}; while ( hub . PopEvent ( e )) { switch ( e . kind ) { case bno08x :: EventKind :: Sensor : std :: printf ( "sensor 0x%02" PRIX32 " at %" PRIu32 " us 
 " , static_cast < uint32_t > ( e . sensor ), e . t_us ); break ; case bno08x :: EventKind :: OpDone : if ( e . op == waiting_for ) { std :: printf ( "operation finished: %s 
 " , bno08x :: ToString ( e . error )); } break ; case bno08x :: EventKind :: Reset : std :: printf ( "the hub restarted: features are sent again 
 " ); break ; default : break ; } } } Events are the one output of the driver. PopEvent() returns false when none is waiting. The kinds: EventKind Meaning Sensor A sample: sensor , accuracy , t_us (host time), v[] in the report's units OpDone An operation finished: op , error , detail , response values in v[] FeatureChanged The hub changed a sensor's rate by itself Reset The hub restarted; features are sent again with auto_restore FlushDone A Flush() completed for sensor HubError The SHTP error list: detail is the first code, v[] all of them Dropped The event queue was full; detail is how many events were lost Rvc A UART-RVC frame Sh2Error An entry of the SH-2 error queue ( ReportErrors() ) Drain the queue at least as often as it fills: the default holds 32 events, so a 100 Hz rotation vector plus a 100 Hz gyroscope fills it in 160 ms. A full queue drops new events and reports how many with one Dropped event rather than overwriting or blocking. Sensors lists every report and its units; Calibration covers tare, calibration and records. Operations ¶ bno08x :: Error CalibrateAndSave ( Hub & hub ) { bno08x :: MeCal cal {}; cal . accel = true ; cal . gyro = true ; cal . mag = true ; if ( const auto r = hub . ConfigureMeCal ( cal ); ! r . ok ()) { return r . error ; } // ... wait for its OpDone, rotate the board until the accuracy reaches High, then: return hub . SaveDcd (). error ; } One operation runs on the wire at a time; up to Limits::kOpQueue wait behind it, and one more returns Busy . An operation that gets no answer ends with Timeout after op_timeout_ms ; a hub restart ends it with HubReset . Reset() restarts the hub's software, HardReset() pulses NRST (it needs the SetReset hook), HubOn() and HubSleep() change the hub's power state, and Initialize() re-initialises the sensor hub. Handle errors ¶ const char * Describe ( bno08x :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case bno08x :: Error :: Bus : return "a port hook returned false: check the wiring, the address and the bus speed" ; case bno08x :: Error :: Timeout : return "the hub did not answer: check power, the reset pin and H_INTN" ; case bno08x :: Error :: Variant : return "the configured chip does not have this feature" ; case bno08x :: Error :: Refused : return "the hub answered with a failure status" ; default : return bno08x :: ToString ( e ); } } Signal Meaning What to do Error::Bus A port hook returned false Check the port, the address and the bus speed Error::Timeout The hub did not answer Check power, NRST and H_INTN; a sensor the board lacks never answers Error::NotInitialized Begin() has not run or the session is not ready Wait for Ready() ; after Faulted call Begin() Error::Variant The configured chip lacks the feature Check Config::variant ; see Ambiguities Error::Busy The operation queue is full Drain events and wait for an OpDone Error::Framing , HubReset Bad bytes or a restart ended the operation Repeat it; if it recurs read GetStats() Error::Refused , DeviceFault The hub's status says no The detail word holds the status Error::Oversize The request does not fit one write Raise Limits::kTxCargo or send less Error::Unsupported The hook or transport cannot do it Add the hook, or use another transport Every value, with the calls that return it, is on the Contract page. bno08x::ToString() names an error for a log. Diagnostics ¶ GetStats() returns counters of everything the driver dropped, repaired or noticed: each framing rule has one, and so do resynchronisations, hub restarts, bus errors, dropped events, and the UART-RVC checksum results. They are never reset by the driver. Advertised() holds what the hub advertised, Product() the product ID after ReadProductId() , and GetMetadata() a sensor's range, resolution and power after ReadMetadata() . TraceLastTransfer() copies the first 32 bytes of the most recent transfer the hub sent (the SHTP header first) and GetLastTransferLength() gives its full length, both without any bus traffic. The driver offers no raw bus read: it would race the framing engine. Next: Configuration .

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: three layers, one of them yours, and what happens in each when a sample arrives. Datasheet sections this page relies on SHTP header, channels and cargo reads: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.3.1 SHTP, p. 22 Report structure, product ID, executable commands: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.3.2 Report Structure, p. 23 Getting started: establishing contact and reading: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 5 Getting started with BNO08X, p. 43 Start-up timing: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 6.5.3 Startup timing, p. 47 Command request and response: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.3.8 Command Request (0xF2), p. 43 Header, channels and the rules of a cargo: CEVA 1000-3535 1.10, 2.2.1 SHTP Header, p. 4 Channel advertisement: CEVA 1000-3535 1.10, 5.2 Channel Advertisement, p. 15 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/bno08x.hpp public calls ; inc/bno08x_interface.hpp HubInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Owns Core inc/bno08x.hpp , src/bno08x.ipp The session state machine, the operation queue, the event queue, timing, errors Protocol inc/bno08x_shtp.hpp , inc/bno08x_rvc.hpp SHTP framing and reassembly, the UART framing, the advertisement, the UART-RVC frames Definitions inc/bno08x_types.hpp , inc/bno08x_registers.hpp , inc/bno08x_reports.hpp , inc/bno08x_records.hpp Error , Result , Config , Event , the SH-2 constants, the table of report layouts, the FRS records Port contract inc/bno08x_interface.hpp The CRTP base, the HubPort concept and its transport variants Platform port Your class The bus or UART, a clock, H_INTN and optionally NRST, BOOTN, WAKE and logging Helpers inc/bno08x_euler.hpp , inc/bno08x_kconfig.hpp Integer quaternion to Euler; an optional Config from ESP-IDF menuconfig Never blocking ¶ The hub is asynchronous: it sends reports when it likes, answers requests later, and batches. The driver is therefore a state machine that you run from your loop. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Idle Idle --> Resetting: Begin(), NRST wired Idle --> WaitAdvert: Begin(), no NRST Idle --> Ready: Begin(), UART-RVC Resetting --> WaitAdvert: reset wait over Resetting --> Faulted: NRST cannot be released WaitAdvert --> WaitReady: advertisement parsed WaitReady --> Ready: reset complete and initialise response WaitAdvert --> Faulted: start-up timeout WaitReady --> Faulted: start-up timeout Ready --> WaitReady: the hub restarted WaitAdvert --> Resetting: HardReset() or framing faults WaitReady --> Resetting: HardReset() or framing faults Ready --> Resetting: HardReset() or framing faults Faulted --> Resetting: Begin() or HardReset() Faulted --> WaitAdvert: Begin(), no NRST Not drawn, to keep the picture readable: Begin() starts again from any state, like from Idle . Without NRST, too many framing faults queue the reset command instead, and the session stays where it is until the hub's restart arrives ( Ready to WaitReady ). A HardReset() or framing-fault reset whose pins cannot be driven leaves the session Faulted . In Faulted only stop requests are written and nothing read is used. Poll(now_us) reads what the hub has waiting (a transfer per H_INTN on I2C and SPI, the bytes in the UART receiver), reassembles cargoes, decodes reports into events, writes the next queued request and checks the timeouts. It never waits on the hub: a port hook that needs time (a stretching bus) is the only thing that can. One sample through the layers ¶ sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant Core as Bno08x participant Port as Your port participant Hub as BNO08x App->>Core: SetFeature(RotationVector, 10 ms) Core-->>App: OpId Core->>Port: I2cWrite(set feature cargo) Hub-->>Port: H_INTN low App->>Core: Poll(now) Core->>Port: IntAsserted(), I2cRead(header, rest) Note over Core: reassemble, timestamp, decode Core-->>App: Event Sensor on PopEvent() Design choices ¶ CRTP and concepts, not virtual functions. Every sensor's layout is one row of a table, checked at compile time; adding a report adds a row. Independent model for tests. docs.text: The hub is asynchronous: it sends reports when it likes, answers requests later, and batches. The driver is therefore a state machine that you run from your loop. stateDiagram-v2 [*] --> Idle Idle --> Resetting: Begin(), NRST wired Idle --> WaitAdvert: Begin(), no NRST Idle --> Ready: Begin(), UART-RVC Resetting --> WaitAdvert: reset wait over Resetting --> Faulted: NRST cannot be released WaitAdvert --> WaitReady: advertisement parsed WaitReady --> Ready: reset complete and initialise response WaitAdvert --> Faulted: start-up timeout WaitReady --> Faulted: start-up timeout Ready --> WaitReady: the hub restarted WaitAdvert --> Resetting: HardReset() or framing faults WaitReady --> Resetting: HardReset() or framing faults Ready --> Resetting: HardReset() or framing faults Faulted --> Resetting: Begin() or HardReset() Faulted --> WaitAdvert: Begin(), no NRST Not drawn, to keep the picture readable: Begin() starts again from any state, like from Idle . Without NRST, too many framing faults queue the reset command instead, and the session stays where it is until the hub's restart arrives ( Ready to WaitReady ). A HardReset() or framing-fault reset whose pins cannot be driven leaves the session Faulted . In Faulted only stop requests are written and nothing read is used. Poll(now_us) reads what the hub has waiting (a transfer per H_INTN on I2C and SPI, the bytes in the UART receiver), reassembles cargoes, decodes reports into events, writes the next queued request and checks the timeouts. It never waits on the hub: a port hook that needs time (a stretching bus) is the only thing that can.

docs.text: Calibration and orientation ¶ How to make the hub's output accurate and keep it that way: the motion engine's calibration, saving it, tare and reorientation, and the flash records behind them. Every call returns an OpId and finishes with an OpDone event ( API guide ). Datasheet sections this page relies on Sensor metadata and the FRS record list: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.3.4 Sensor Metadata, p. 25 Calibration and its accuracy: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 3.1 Calibration Effects, p. 37 Interactive calibration (BNO086 only): CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 3.3 Interactive Calibration (BNO086 only), p. 39 Orientation and tare: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 4 BNO08X orientation, p. 40 Configuration records: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 4.3 Records, p. 14 Sensor metadata record layout: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 5.1 Sensor Metadata, p. 30 Interactive calibration: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 5.6 Interactive Calibration, p. 36 FRS write and read: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.3.3 FRS Write Request (0xF7), p. 40 Tare now and persist tare: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.4.3 Tare (0x03), p. 47 Dynamic calibration data and ME calibration: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.4.5 Save DCD (0x06), p. 51 Simple calibration, interactive calibration, wheel: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.4.10 Simple Calibration Commands (0x0C), p. 55 Calibration procedure and user calibration: CEVA 1000-4044 1.6, 3.0 User Calibration, p. 5 Tare options and procedure: CEVA 1000-4045 1.3, Tare Overview, p. 1 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Dynamic calibration ¶ The motion engine calibrates the accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer while the board moves. Each sensor reports its state as an accuracy ( Accuracy::Unreliable to High ) on every sample, and a rotation vector also carries an estimated angular error. The calibration guides describe the movements that bring each sensor to high accuracy; nothing in the driver speeds them up. ConfigureMeCal(MeCal) chooses which sensors calibrate ( accel , gyro , mag , and the planar and on_table variants); GetMeCal() returns the current enables in the OpDone values. SaveDcd() writes the calibration data to flash so the next start begins calibrated, SetPeriodicDcd(true) has the hub do that on its own, and ClearDcdAndReset() throws it away and restarts the hub. The periodic-save flag is inverted in the protocol (0 enables); the API takes a plain bool (A35). bno08x :: Error CalibrateAndSave ( Hub & hub ) { bno08x :: MeCal cal {}; cal . accel = true ; cal . gyro = true ; cal . mag = true ; if ( const auto r = hub . ConfigureMeCal ( cal ); ! r . ok ()) { return r . error ; } // ... wait for its OpDone, rotate the board until the accuracy reaches High, then: return hub . SaveDcd (). error ; } Tare and reorientation ¶ A tare declares the current pose to be the reference. Tare(AxisMask, TareBasis) takes the axes ( All or ZOnly ; the other masks are refused unless Config::tare_any_mask is set, A37) and the rotation vector the tare is based on. A tare on the game rotation vector reorients only that vector and is not persistent. PersistTare() keeps the last tare over a restart. SetReorientation(Quat14) and ClearReorientation() set the mounting orientation, a fixed rotation applied to every output. bno08x :: Error TareHeading ( Hub & hub ) { if ( const auto r = hub . Tare ( bno08x :: AxisMask :: ZOnly , bno08x :: TareBasis :: RotationVector ); ! r . ok ()) { return r . error ; } return hub . PersistTare (). error ; // optional: keep it over a restart } Interactive calibration (BNO086) ¶ The BNO086 can be told what the host knows about its motion: SetMotionIntent(MotionIntent) with the states unknown, stationary (with or without vibration), in motion and in motion accelerating. The hub asks for the information through sensor 0x2B ( MotionRequest ), and StartSimpleCal() and FinishSimpleCal() run the simple calibration, whose result is in the finish operation's detail ( SimpleCalStatus ). On a BNO080 or BNO085 the driver refuses these with Error::Variant while Config::strict_variant is set (A3, A4). Records in flash (FRS) ¶ The hub keeps its configuration in numbered records. ReadFrs(record, FrsBuffer&) fills a caller-owned buffer of up to kFrsMaxWords words, which must stay valid until the OpDone event; WriteFrs() writes words and, with Config::frs_verify , reads them back; EraseFrs() erases. One FRS operation runs at a time (A29). A write is complete at status 3; status 12 means the memory is full (A26, A27). Reads send zero in the reserved bytes (A28). Sensor metadata ( ReadMetadata , GetMetadata ) lives in per-sensor records and is parsed in both layout revisions (A30). bno08x :: Error ReadOrientationRecord ( Hub & hub ) { static bno08x :: FrsBuffer buffer ; // must stay valid until the OpDone event return hub . ReadFrs ( 0x2D3E , buffer ). error ; // the words are in `buffer` when the operation finishes } Writing a record the driver does not describe can change how the hub behaves in ways only a restart undoes. Use the typed calls above where one exists. Next: Ambiguities .

docs.text: Configuration ¶ Config holds everything you choose about a session; Limits sizes the buffers. A Config{} is the recommended setup for a BNO085 on I2C address 0x4A. The chip is never detected, so say which one you have. Fields ¶ Fields with a unit carry it in the name. Config::Valid() checks a configuration without touching the chip, and Begin() calls it first and returns InvalidArgument with nothing sent. Field Default Meaning variant Bno085 The chip: Bno080 , Bno085 or Bno086 ; selects behaviour (A1) read_policy HeaderThenRest I2C and SPI: read the header, then exactly the rest; or Fixed bytes per read i2c_address 0x4A 0x4A (SA0 low) or 0x4B (SA0 high) fixed_read_bytes 64 Bytes per read for Fixed , 4 to 1024 strict_variant true Refuse features the chip lacks with Variant (A3) auto_restore true Send the enabled features again after the hub restarts poll_without_int false Guarded, I2C only: read on a cadence without H_INTN (A2) require_init_response true Wait for the hub's initialise response at start (A11) frs_verify true Read an FRS record back after writing it set_feature_confirm false Finish SetFeature on the hub's reply, not when written strict_raw false Refuse a raw sensor while its base sensor is off strict_cont_len true Require continuation length = remaining + 4 (A14) strict_padding false Count non-zero padding bytes tare_any_mask false Allow tare axis masks other than all axes and Z only (A37) rvc_strict false UART-RVC: also require the index to increment by one rvc_inputs_experimental false Guarded: allow the unverified $MIB text inputs (A8) startup_timeout_ms 500 Limit for each start-up wait op_timeout_ms 1000 Limit for one operation frs_write_timeout_ms 5000 Limit for one FRS write step wake_timeout_us 10000 SPI: limit for H_INTN after WAKE reset_pulse_us 1000 NRST low time; the datasheet minimum is 10 ns advert_retry_ms 100 Without NRST: wait before asking for the advertisement again uart_token_timeout_ms 1000 UART-SHTP: BSN validity when the hub did not advertise one uart_bsq_retry_ms 20 UART-SHTP: wait for a BSN before the query is sent again poll_interval_ms 10 poll_without_int : read cadence resync_limit 4 Framing violations within the window that force a recovery resync_window_ms 100 The window of resync_limit product_id_entries 1 Product ID responses that complete a request, 1 to 5 (A33); Product() is entry 0 Config::Valid() is false when an enumeration holds a value that is not an enumerator, the address is neither 0x4A nor 0x4B , fixed_read_bytes is outside 4 to 1024, a timeout, reset_pulse_us , uart_bsq_retry_ms or the resync window is zero, wake_timeout_us is not shorter than op_timeout_ms (so WAKE is always released before an operation ends), or product_id_entries is outside 1 to 5. bno08x :: Config BnoOnSa0High () { bno08x :: Config c {}; // the recommended setup for a BNO085 c . variant = bno08x :: Variant :: Bno086 ; // chosen by you: the chip is never detected c . i2c_address = bno08x :: reg :: kI2cAddrHigh ; // SA0 tied high c . set_feature_confirm = true ; // SetFeature finishes on the hub's own reply c . op_timeout_ms = 400 ; return c ; // c.Valid() checks it without the chip } struct SmallLimits { static constexpr std :: size_t kRxCargo = 512 ; // at least 256 static constexpr std :: size_t kTxCargo = 64 ; // at least 24 static constexpr std :: size_t kOpQueue = 4 ; static constexpr std :: size_t kEventQueue = 16 ; }; bno08x :: Error StartSmall ( MyPort & port ) { static bno08x :: Bno08x < MyPort , SmallLimits > hub ( port ); // the buffers live inside the object return hub . Begin ( BnoOnSa0High ()). error ; // InvalidArgument if a field is out of range } Limits ¶ Bno08x<Port, Limits> keeps every buffer inside the object; Limits gives the sizes at compile time and a static_assert rejects values the protocol cannot work with. Member Default Minimum Meaning kRxCargo 1024 256 Largest cargo received, in bytes kTxCargo 128 24 Largest cargo sent, header included kOpQueue 8 2 Operations pending at once; one more returns Busy kEventQueue 32 4 Events waiting for PopEvent() ; a full queue drops and counts ( Dropped ) Kconfig ¶ Under ESP-IDF, idf.py menuconfig shows BNO08x sensor hub when the driver is a component of the project ( Installation ); the menu is _config/Kconfig . The options reach the code only through inc/bno08x_kconfig.hpp , never through a driver signature: bno08x :: Error StartFromMenuconfig ( MyPort & port ) { static bno08x :: Bno08x < MyPort , bno08x :: KconfigLimits > hub ( port ); return hub . Begin ( bno08x :: KconfigDefaults ()). error ; } Option Default Effect CONFIG_BNO08X_VARIANT_* BNO085 Config::variant CONFIG_BNO08X_I2C_ADDR_HIGH n i2c_address 0x4B CONFIG_BNO08X_NOT_STRICT_VARIANT n strict_variant false CONFIG_BNO08X_NO_AUTO_RESTORE n auto_restore false CONFIG_BNO08X_SET_FEATURE_CONFIRM n set_feature_confirm CONFIG_BNO08X_RX_CARGO , _TX_CARGO 1024, 128 KconfigLimits CONFIG_BNO08X_OP_QUEUE , _EVENT_QUEUE 8, 32 KconfigLimits CONFIG_BNO08X_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS , _OP_TIMEOUT_MS 500, 1000 the two timeouts Without Kconfig (plain CMake, other platforms) KconfigDefaults() returns Config{} . Both cases are host tests. Next: Porting .

docs.text: Contract ¶ What the BNO08x driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the port and does no I/O. Begin(Config) validates the configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the port up and starts the reset; it returns at once. Poll(now_us) does everything else: the reset wait, the advertisement, the initialise handshake. Ready() turns true when the session is up. Every other call returns Error::NotInitialized until then, and again after a start-up step timed out ( State::Faulted , which only Begin() and HardReset() leave); the stop requests below are the exception. Begin() again, in any state, starts a new session: every operation still waiting ends with NotInitialized (its OpDone is queued with the events already waiting, which stay for PopEvent() ). No call blocks. A call that needs the hub queues an operation and returns its OpId ; the outcome arrives as an OpDone event. Every operation ends with Timeout at worst: its limit ( Config::op_timeout_ms , an FRS write's answer frs_write_timeout_ms ) starts when it reaches the head of the queue, so one queued behind others may wait up to the queue length times that. A stop queued before the session is up waits for it, which startup_timeout_ms bounds. The limits are elapsed times: a long gap between Poll() calls ends an operation at the next one. Every failed port write ends its operation with Error::Bus . A failed read in Poll() is counted in Stats::bus_errors and the session stays Ready ; it is never turned into a sample, and no event reports it, so watch the counter when the link may fail. The driver never fragments a write and never sends a request larger than one transfer ( Oversize ). The framing engine follows the SHTP rules strictly, counts every violation in Stats and resets the hub after resync_limit of them within resync_window_ms (with NRST through it, without through the reset command, which the driver writes itself). Operations in flight end with Framing . A duplicate SHTP sequence number drops the transfer, except a new cargo on channel 0 or 1 (the advertisement, command responses, the reset-complete): after a restart every channel numbers from 0 again. After the hub restarts by itself the driver reports a Reset event, abandons running operations with HubReset , starts the host sequence numbers again and, with Config::auto_restore , enables the sensors again. A restart is seen through its advertisement, or through a reset-complete or initialise response the session already had (the boot's own may follow an answered advertisement within startup_timeout_ms of Ready ). Only an enable the driver saw finish with Ok is remembered for restoring, and the newest request for a sensor has the last word: a failed or abandoned one is not sent again. A restore write that fails is tried three more times, then counted in Stats::restore_failed . Ok means written when set_feature_confirm is false and accepted when it is true. Stop requests (switching a sensor off with SetFeature and interval_us == 0 , Reset() , HubSleep() ) always act once Begin() has run, in every state and whatever the other fields hold: before the session is ready they wait for it (without NRST the driver's request for the advertisement goes ahead of them and may use the kept slot; a queue already full of stops leaves it no room, so the start-up times out); in Faulted they are written at once and complete when written; a stop queued when a start-up step times out still goes out. The last queue slot is kept for them; when the queue is full, the newest operation that has not started ends with Busy to make room; the same stop asked again while it waits returns the operation it already has, but only while it is still the newest request for its target (the sensor's feature, or the hub's power state: Reset() , HubSleep() , HubOn() ), so off, on, off ends off. A stop gets Busy only when every queued operation is a stop, an internal request or the one being sent. A sensor switched off is forgotten by the restore list at once. Entering Faulted releases WAKE and closes a half-sent UART frame first, so the stops that follow reach the hub; a written Reset() restarts the sequence numbers, in Faulted too. Reset pins that cannot be driven ( HardReset() , the NRST release of a reset, the reset of a resynchronisation) leave the session Faulted with Error::Bus ; no Reset event is reported for a restart that did not happen. An advertised report length shorter than the 4-byte report header is refused (the built-in length is kept) and counted in Stats::bad_advert . A feature the configured chip lacks returns Error::Variant without sending anything (unless strict_variant is false). The UART-RVC transport accepts no command and returns Unsupported for them. An unknown SensorId returns InvalidArgument ; no input crashes the driver. The fuzz target feeds arbitrary bytes on every transport, including UART frames longer than the receive buffer, which are dropped and counted in Stats::oversize_frame . A missing mandatory hook is a compile error; a missing optional hook ( SetReset , SetBootn , TakeIntTimestamp , Log ) changes a documented behaviour and never compiles away silently. A misdeclared hook is a compile error that names it. Firmware update and the bootloader are not supported. Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates bno08x_version.h Your port The bus, a clock, H_INTN, and optionally NRST, BOOTN and logging ( Porting ) Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the org. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Call Poll() and every other method from one task, or guard every call on one object with a mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when other chips share the bus. A port's TakeIntTimestamp() may read a value an interrupt wrote, so make that access atomic. Nothing else may run in an interrupt. Separate objects share no state. Errors ¶ bno08x::Error inside bno08x::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; values from 16 are specific to this driver. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 Begin() has not run, or the session is not ready, or it faulted InvalidArgument 2 An argument or a Config field is out of range; nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false Timeout 4 The hub did not answer in the allowed time DeviceIdMismatch 5 Never returned: the chip has no ID register Crc 6 Never returned: no link of this chip carries a CRC Busy 7 The operation queue is full (a stop request may displace a waiting operation, which then ends with Busy ) DeviceFault 8 The hub reported a failure in a response Unsupported 9 The hook or feature the call needs is absent (a command on UART-RVC, HardReset() without SetReset ) Framing 16 A frame rule was broken and the engine resynchronised HubReset 17 The hub restarted; the operation was abandoned Overflow 18 The event queue or a cargo buffer was full Refused 19 The hub answered with a failure status Oversize 20 A request does not fit one write; nothing was sent NotAdvertised 21 The channel or report was never advertised by the hub Variant 22 The feature is not available on the configured chip The API guide says what to do about each. Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. Every buffer is a member of the driver object, sized by Limits ( Configuration ); the largest are the receive cargo and the event queue. The UART-SHTP transport adds frame buffers of twice the cargo sizes for the escaped bytes, and one chunk the UART transports read into (a member, so a DMA-filled read never lands in a dead stack frame). Nothing is allocated after construction. Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ None.

If you have a newer revision, compare its revision history with the topics above; a change to a pin, a register, a timing or a value the driver uses is a bug report for this repository. Where the driver deliberately goes beyond the datasheet, the Contract says so. The repository never contains the PDF itself: vendors own their documents. Download it from the vendor, and compare its SHA-256 with the one above to confirm you have the same file.

docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own port, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the driver on any PC against a model of the hub, on every transport, with eleven programs: a quickstart, one per transport, calibration, tare, batching, records, metadata, the step counter and fault tolerance. No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/bno08x_example_i2c_quickstart The host tests build the folder with warnings as errors and run every program (CTest bno08x_example_<name> ). ESP32 ¶ ESP-IDF applications that run the driver on an ESP32-C6 DevKitC-1 over I2C; the wiring is in the example folder's README and the port in esp32_bno08x_port.hpp . The project points EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at the repository root, which is the driver's ESP-IDF component. The apps ¶ App What it shows Source CI bno08x_basic_example Start a BNO08x on I2C, enable the rotation vector at 50 Hz and log yaw, pitch and roll bno08x_basic_example.cpp yes Build and flash one (from examples/esp32 , ESP-IDF environment loaded): ./scripts/build_app.sh bno08x_basic_example Release ./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor bno08x_basic_example Release Source of this table: examples/esp32/app_config.yml . Set up once ¶ git submodule update --init examples/esp32/scripts # the ESP-IDF build scripts cd examples/esp32 . $IDF_PATH /export.sh # ESP-IDF v5.5 ./scripts/build_app.sh list # every app and build type The scripts read app_config.yml (the same file this page's table comes from) and build each app as its own firmware image. What to read in an example ¶ You want to Read See the Begin() and Poll() loop with events bno08x_basic_example.cpp Write an ESP-IDF port with the interrupt timestamp esp32_bno08x_port.hpp Use menuconfig values bno08x_kconfig.hpp and _config/Kconfig

docs.text: Hardware ¶ The BNO08x's package, pins, host-interface straps, supplies, timing and reference circuits, as the driver uses them. The three chips share one package and one pinout; they differ in firmware features only ( Ambiguities ). Datasheet sections this page relies on Features, variants and what differs: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, Features (front page), p. 1 Protocol selection (PS1, PS0): CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.2 BNO08X Connectivity, p. 9 Pins, straps and the clock source: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.2.1 Pin Descriptions, p. 10 I2C: address, clock stretching, framing: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.2.2 I2C interface, p. 12 Supplies, absolute maximum ratings and power management: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 6.1 Absolute Maximum Electrical Ratings, p. 45 Start-up timing: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 6.5.3 Startup timing, p. 47 Package outline and landing pattern: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 7.1 Package Outline, p. 53 Pin and interface differences from the BNO070: CEVA (Hillcrest Labs) none printed 1.6, 2.1 Pinout Comparisons, p. 7 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Package and pins ¶ A 28-pin LGA, body 5.2 x 3.8 mm, nominal height 1.1 mm, moisture sensitivity level 1, lead-free reflow up to 260 °C (data sheet section 7). Pin 1 is at the top right of the top view and the numbers run counter-clockwise. BNO08x pinout, LGA-28 Figure description and sources The BNO08x seen from the top, in its LGA-28 package. Pin 1 is marked by the dot; the numbers run counter-clockwise from it. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Source of this table and of the chip figures: docs/hardware.yml . Choosing the host interface ¶ Two strap pins, PS1 and PS0, and BOOTN are sampled at reset and choose the host interface. The driver does not detect it: the port you write names the transport ( kTransport ) and the wiring must agree. PS1 PS0 Host interface Driver transport 0 0 I2C Transport::I2c 0 1 UART-RVC Transport::UartRvc 1 0 UART with SHTP Transport::UartShtp 1 1 SPI Transport::Spi BOOTN must be high at reset for the application to start; it needs a 10 kΩ pull-up (a low level starts the bootloader, which this driver does not support). SPI needs both strap pins high from before reset until after the first H_INTN, and PS0 must be a GPIO because it becomes the WAKE input afterwards. The clock source is chosen by CLKSEL0 and CLKSEL1 at reset: a 32.768 kHz crystal (CLKSEL0 low or open), an external clock on pin 27 (both high), or the internal oscillator (CLKSEL0 high, CLKSEL1 low or open). The internal oscillator must not be used with either UART mode ; I2C and SPI tolerate it. The environmental sensor bus pins ENV_SCL and ENV_SDA need pull-ups even when no sensor is fitted. Pin hooks ¶ Pin Port hook What the driver does with it NRST SetReset(bool) Pulses it low at Begin() and HardReset() ; without it the driver asks the running hub for its advertisement H_INTN IntAsserted() Reads only when it is low (I2C, SPI); on UART it is optional H_INTN edge TakeIntTimestamp(uint32_t&) Optional: the time of the edge, for exact sample timestamps PS0/WAKE SetWake(bool) SPI: pulls it low before a write BOOTN SetBootn(bool) Optional: held high during the reset sequence Timing ¶ Parameter Value Driver NRST pulse at least 10 ns Config::reset_pulse_us (default 1 ms) Internal initialisation after reset t1 at least 90 ms, then t2 about 4 ms Config::startup_timeout_ms bounds each wait H_INTN after WAKE (SPI) 150 µs typical Config::wake_timeout_us Host answer to H_INTN within about 10 ms, or the hub gives up and raises it again Poll() should run every few milliseconds ( Transports ) UART-SHTP host bytes at least 100 µs apart The driver paces them; or your port does SPI clock mode 3, up to 3 MHz Your port I2C clock 100 or 400 kHz; the hub stretches the clock Your port Supplies ¶ VDD 2.4 V to 3.6 V powers the sensors; VDDIO 1.7 V to 3.6 V powers the core and the I/O (the pin table says 1.65 V; the operating-conditions table, which the driver's documentation follows, says 1.7 V). VDD must be on before or together with VDDIO. Put 100 nF at each supply pin and 100 nF from CAP to GND. docs.title: Package and pins

docs.text: Two strap pins, PS1 and PS0, and BOOTN are sampled at reset and choose the host interface. The driver does not detect it: the port you write names the transport ( kTransport ) and the wiring must agree. PS1 PS0 Host interface Driver transport 0 0 I2C Transport::I2c 0 1 UART-RVC Transport::UartRvc 1 0 UART with SHTP Transport::UartShtp 1 1 SPI Transport::Spi BOOTN must be high at reset for the application to start; it needs a 10 kΩ pull-up (a low level starts the bootloader, which this driver does not support). SPI needs both strap pins high from before reset until after the first H_INTN, and PS0 must be a GPIO because it becomes the WAKE input afterwards. The clock source is chosen by CLKSEL0 and CLKSEL1 at reset: a 32.768 kHz crystal (CLKSEL0 low or open), an external clock on pin 27 (both high), or the internal oscillator (CLKSEL0 high, CLKSEL1 low or open). The internal oscillator must not be used with either UART mode ; I2C and SPI tolerate it. The environmental sensor bus pins ENV_SCL and ENV_SDA need pull-ups even when no sensor is fitted.

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( bno08x_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-bno08x.git external/driver-bno08x git submodule update --init external/driver-bno08x Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-bno08x ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE bno08x::bno08x ) bno08x::bno08x is an alias of the bno08x INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect BNO08X_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver BNO08X_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-bno08x -B build-bno08x cmake --install build-bno08x --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( bno08x 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE bno08x::bno08x ) The target is bno08x::bno08x in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated bno08x_version.h go to include/bno08x/inc/ , the template implementation to include/bno08x/src/bno08x.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-bno08x) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-bno08x (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-bno08x.git components/bno08x bno08x (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml bno08x (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : bno08x : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-bno08x.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES bno08x (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. docs.text: Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build.
docs.title: Installation

docs.text: A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( bno08x_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result .
docs.title: Requirements

docs.text: A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-bno08x.git external/driver-bno08x git submodule update --init external/driver-bno08x Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ).
docs.title: Get the source

docs.text: This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-bno08x ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE bno08x::bno08x ) bno08x::bno08x is an alias of the bno08x INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect BNO08X_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver BNO08X_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI )
docs.title: CMake (any MCU, any host)

docs.text: To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-bno08x -B build-bno08x cmake --install build-bno08x --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( bno08x 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE bno08x::bno08x ) The target is bno08x::bno08x in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated bno08x_version.h go to include/bno08x/inc/ , the template implementation to include/bno08x/src/bno08x.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ).
