docs.title: Index

docs.text: Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?"
docs.title: RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset

docs.text: Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?"
docs.title: RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read

docs.text: Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?"
docs.title: RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data

docs.text: Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?"
docs.title: RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something

docs.text: Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends."
docs.title: RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused

docs.text: Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?"
docs.title: RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack

docs.text: Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?"
docs.title: RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading

docs.text: Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?"
docs.title: RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard

docs.text: Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?"
docs.title: RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard

docs.text: Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b.
docs.title: RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read

docs.text: Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?"
docs.title: RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing

docs.text: Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?"
docs.title: RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit

docs.text: Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return.
docs.title: RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks

docs.text: Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample.
docs.title: RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim

docs.text: Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09.
docs.title: RD-32 Docs style

docs.text: Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py .
docs.title: RD-33 Another project's name or dated history

docs.text: Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes.
docs.title: RD-25 Guards no test kills

docs.text: Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?"
docs.title: RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules

docs.text: Rule: a call in a test or fuzz target takes, as separate arguments, no operation that changes state together with a read of that state ( sent() , Transfers() , pending() , a flag, a counter, a clock). The order of the arguments of a call, of the operands of + - == < and of the two sides of an assignment is unspecified; GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left, Clang and GCC on aarch64 left to right. Braced-init lists, && , || , ?: and , are sequenced. Two reads of the fuzzer's input ( in.Byte() , FuzzConfig(in) ) in one expression count as well: they advance the input, so the same corpus file decodes into different calls per compiler. // bad: x86-64 GCC reads sent() before the call, so it is always 0 here Check ( d . Write ( v ), was_up , sent ()); // good: the result first, then the read; or pass the probe and read it inside the helper, after the call const auto r = d . Write ( v ); Check ( r , was_up , sent ()); Hurts: the check passes, or aborts, on one CI runner only. A "nothing was sent" promise becomes vacuous, and a positive promise ( sent >= 1 ) aborts on a correct driver; neither shows on an Apple-silicon or aarch64 rehearsal. Seen: dynamixel (first CI, sent >= 1 aborted on x86-64 GCC only), pcal9555 (three fuzz cases, latent), tle92466ed (16 fuzz cases, vacuous; 6 more with two input reads), the template's own fuzz target (5 cases). 3 drivers, all copies of the same pattern. Detection: lint ( enforced ): tools/eval_order_check.py , the eval-order preflight step, scans tests/ and examples/ . test : the fuzz replay with a one-edit mutant that must abort ( mutant_replay_* , kept out of the fuzz_* names so the libFuzzer job does not pick it up).
docs.title: RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check

docs.text: Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit.
docs.title: RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate.
docs.title: RD-19 Template drift

docs.text: Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count).
docs.title: RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI

docs.text: Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep).
docs.title: RD-11 Header outside the library subset

docs.text: Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != .
docs.title: RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic

docs.text: Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests .
docs.title: RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses

docs.text: Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned).
docs.title: RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended.
docs.title: RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp .
docs.title: RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ

docs.text: Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?"
docs.title: RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type

docs.text: Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision.
docs.title: RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2

docs.text: Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call.
docs.title: RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete

docs.text: Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?"
docs.title: RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults

docs.text: Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert .
docs.title: RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler

docs.text: Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. Make it public ( gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences ), then python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply : rulesets, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL and private vulnerability reporting need a public repository. If the last call answers 422, run it again after a few seconds; the new visibility has not reached that endpoint yet. Enable Pages from the gh-pages branch, root, and open https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/ . --check reports 0 change(s) pending . A private repository on the free plan shares a small Actions storage quota with the rest of its organisation. A full quota fails every upload step in every repository of it at once, which looks like a broken workflow and is not one; a public repository does not count against it.

docs.text: Sensors ¶ Every sensor report ID that a CEVA document defines has a typed event. The chip itself implements a subset; the rest is described in the reference manual only and is allowed but may never answer (A31). Datasheet sections this page relies on Configuration and the commands list: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.3.3 BNO08X Configuration, p. 24 Sensor reports, timestamps and batching: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.3.5 Sensor Reports, p. 26 Motion, orientation and environmental outputs: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 2 Sensor data processing, p. 30 Report rates and latency: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 6.9 Report Rates, p. 50 Feature reports, rate and batch: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 5.4 Feature Reports, p. 34 Sensor report common fields and status: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.5.1 Common Fields, p. 62 Common dynamic feature report: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 6.5.2 Common Dynamic Feature Report, p. 63 Batching and batch timestamps: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 7 Batching, p. 91 SH-2 channel usage and report lengths: CEVA 1000-3600 1.6, 2.2 SH-2 Channel Usage, p. 4 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Turn a sensor on and read it ¶ SetFeature(id, FeatureConfig) enables a report at interval_us ; zero turns it off. The call returns an OpId and the sample events arrive through PopEvent() . With Config::set_feature_confirm the operation finishes when the hub's own feature response arrives, otherwise when the request has been written. A sensor the hub cannot serve (the environmental sensors without their parts, A20) never produces samples; use GetFeature() to see what the hub actually runs. bno08x :: Error EnableBatched ( Hub & hub ) { bno08x :: FeatureConfig fc {}; fc . interval_us = 10000 ; // 100 Hz fc . batch_us = 100000 ; // deliver in groups every 100 ms return hub . SetFeature ( bno08x :: SensorId :: GyroscopeCalibrated , fc ). error ; } FeatureConfig also carries batch_us (the hub collects samples and delivers them in groups), change_enable and the change sensitivity ( relative selects relative or absolute), wake (the sensor wakes the host) and the sensor-specific word. Flush(id) makes the hub deliver what it holds; FlushDone says it did. Feature(id) returns the last configuration the hub confirmed and Latest(id) the last sample. What an event holds ¶ An Event of kind Sensor has the sensor , its accuracy , the host time t_us , the report's own sequence number and v[] , the report's fields as signed 32-bit integers in the report's own unit. The Q point is the position of the binary point: a Q8 value is the integer divided by 256. The helpers ToMmPerS2 , ToMilliRadPerS , ToNanoTesla , ToMicroRad and ToPpm give whole units with integer arithmetic, and ToEulerCentiDeg() turns a rotation vector into yaw, pitch and roll in centidegrees ( Ambiguities says how accurate it is). Sample times follow the hub's own delay fields: the host time of the interrupt that announced the cargo, minus the delay the cargo reports (base timestamp plus the report's delay). A port that implements TakeIntTimestamp() gives the exact edge time; without it the time of the Poll() that saw H_INTN is used, which is coarser. A base timestamp that signals overflow is counted ( base_overflow ) and the interrupt time is used (A17). ID Sensor v[] Unit (Q) 0x01 Accelerometer x, y, z m/s2 (Q8) 0x02 Gyroscope, calibrated x, y, z rad/s (Q9) 0x03 Magnetic field, calibrated x, y, z uT (Q4) 0x04 Linear acceleration x, y, z m/s2 (Q8) 0x05 Rotation vector i, j, k, real, accuracy unit (Q14), rad (Q12) 0x06 Gravity x, y, z m/s2 (Q8) 0x07 Gyroscope, uncalibrated x, y, z, bias x, y, z rad/s (Q9) 0x08 Game rotation vector i, j, k, real unit (Q14) 0x09 Geomagnetic rotation vector i, j, k, real, accuracy unit (Q14), rad (Q12) 0x0A Pressure value hPa (Q20) 0x0B Ambient light value lux (Q8) 0x0C Humidity value percent (Q8) 0x0D Proximity value cm (Q4) 0x0E Temperature value degrees C (Q7) 0x0F Magnetic field, uncalibrated x, y, z, bias x, y, z uT (Q4) 0x10 Tap detector flags bits 0x11 Step counter latency, steps 100 us ticks, count (16 bit, A18) 0x12 Significant motion flag event 0x13 Stability classifier class enumeration 0x14 Raw accelerometer x, y, z, hub timestamp ADC counts, us 0x15 Raw gyroscope x, y, z, temperature, hub timestamp ADC counts, us 0x16 Raw magnetometer x, y, z, hub timestamp ADC counts, us 0x18 Step detector latency 100 us ticks 0x19 Shake detector axis bits bits 0x1A Flip detector flag event (manual only) 0x1B Pickup detector flag event (manual only) 0x1C Stability detector flag event 0x1E Personal activity classifier page, most likely, 10 confidences enumeration, percent 0x1F Sleep detector state enumeration (manual only) 0x20 to 0x22 Tilt, pocket and circle detectors flag event (manual only) 0x23 Heart rate monitor rate beats per minute (manual only) 0x28 AR/VR rotation vector i, j, k, real, accuracy unit (Q14), rad (Q12) 0x29 AR/VR game rotation vector i, j, k, real unit (Q14) 0x2A Gyro-integrated rotation vector i, j, k, real, rate x, y, z quaternion Q14; rates as in the manual (channel 5, no report ID) 0x2B Motion request intent, request BNO086 interactive calibration 0x2C Optical flow documented fields only manual only; several fields undocumented 0x2D Dead reckoning pose hub timestamp and 13 words Q15 and others, manual only 0x2E Wheel encoder input none named by one library only, no layout; never decoded The reports of 0x2C and 0x2D, and the detectors marked manual only, are implemented from the reference manual and have never been seen from a chip; see Ambiguities . Variants and the report set ¶ The data sheet lists the reports the hubs implement (marked "D" in the working notes); the manual adds more. Config::strict_raw refuses a raw sensor while its base sensor is off. An environmental sensor needs the parts on the hub's secondary I2C bus (a pressure sensor, a light and proximity sensor), which are optional on the board. Rates and latency ¶ Report intervals are in microseconds. The hub rounds to what its sensors can do and answers with the rate it chose; read it with GetFeature() . Batching trades latency for fewer interrupts, and Poll() should run at least once per tenth of the fastest report period, because the hub gives up on a host that answers H_INTN much later than that (A38). Next: Calibration .

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against an independent model of the hub on every transport, a fuzzer that corrupts what the hub sends, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against tests/model/bno08x_hub_model.hpp , a model of the hub written from the CEVA documents and not from the driver. The model speaks SHTP and SH-2 on the four transports: it advertises, resets, accepts feature requests and produces reports, answers commands and FRS requests, fragments cargoes, escapes UART frames, streams UART-RVC frames, and injects faults (bus errors, dropped or delayed H_INTN, bad lengths, wrong sequence numbers, corrupted escapes, bad checksums, restarts in the middle of an operation). Its Knobs struct has one switch for each reading of an ambiguity ( Ambiguities ), so each decision is shown to work and to fail when the hub reads the other way. The tests build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DBNO08X_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_session.cpp Start-up on every transport, the state machine, restarts and recovery tests/test_i2c.cpp , test_spi.cpp The synchronous transports: H_INTN gating, WAKE, header-then-rest reads, padding tests/test_uart_shtp.cpp , test_rvc.cpp Framing, escapes, BSQ and BSN tokens, the 100 us gap, the RVC frames and their checksum tests/test_shtp_frames.cpp Every framing rule V1 to V16 and its counter tests/test_sensors.cpp , test_timestamps.cpp Report layouts and Q points, batching, timestamps and wrap-around tests/test_commands.cpp , test_control.cpp , test_frs.cpp Commands, calibration, tare, FRS read and write tests/test_variants.cpp , test_conformance.cpp The chip differences and the conformance cases of the ambiguities tests/test_errors.cpp The base Error values are 0 to 9; every chip-specific value is returned by some call; invalid input tests/test_units.cpp , test_version.cpp , test_kconfig.cpp Unit helpers and the Euler conversion, the version getters, KconfigDefaults() tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a class that is not a port, a missing hook, a hook without noexcept or with a narrowed parameter, a wrong optional hook, a Limits that is too small tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( bno08x_fuzz_bno08x_corpus ), see below examples/host/ Every host example, built with the test flags and run ( bno08x_example_<name> ) tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds tests/install_consumer/ with find_package(bno08x) tests/check_doxygen.cmake Doxygen with _config/Doxyfile and warnings as errors, when doxygen is installed The model stands alone ¶ The model does not include the driver's definition headers. Its constants (report IDs, command codes, field offsets, timing) are its own, taken from the documents with their sections, so a wrong constant in the driver cannot hide behind the same wrong constant in the model. When a test fails, check the section the model names, and fix the one that is wrong. Every behaviour a bench run shows becomes a knob of the model and a test that fails on the code before the fix. Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver reads comes from the hub over a link a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken hub controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_bno08x.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a transport, a variant and a configuration, then a script of driver calls, and on every transfer what the link does: pass it to the model, flip bits, replace it with the fuzzer's bytes or fail it. After every call it checks the driver's promises (F1 to F11) and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines and a value-initialised result (F1); an operation is accepted only in Ready (never on UART-RVC), except a stop request (switch-off, Reset() , HubSleep() ), which after Begin() is never NotInitialized and is Busy only while the queue holds at least kOpQueue - 3 stops; InvalidArgument sends nothing (F2); every accepted operation yields exactly one OpDone , never for an unknown or finished id (F3); the events between two polls never exceed the queue plus its Dropped marker, and each has a defined kind and sensor (F4, F5); the Stats counters never decrease (F6); Faulted is left only by Begin() or HardReset() (F7); Latest() and Feature() never fail for a defined sensor once ready and never read out of bounds (F8); the Euler conversion of any quaternion stays in range (F9); an FRS read never reports more words than the buffer holds (F10); everything works with a clock that starts just below the 32-bit wrap (F11); on SPI, PS0/WAKE is high at every NRST edge and until the first H_INTN after it (F12); on UART-SHTP the model may drop Buffer Status Notifications, and writes still go out (F13). # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DBNO08X_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DBNO08X_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_bno08x ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_bno08x -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_bno08x The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_bno08x , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_bno08x/ on GCC and Clang ( bno08x_fuzz_bno08x_corpus ): the seeds for every transport, and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ). Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, reported in the step summary Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DBNO08X_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DBNO08X_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( bno08x_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/bno08x.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. docs.text: The tests build the real driver against tests/model/bno08x_hub_model.hpp , a model of the hub written from the CEVA documents and not from the driver. The model speaks SHTP and SH-2 on the four transports: it advertises, resets, accepts feature requests and produces reports, answers commands and FRS requests, fragments cargoes, escapes UART frames, streams UART-RVC frames, and injects faults (bus errors, dropped or delayed H_INTN, bad lengths, wrong sequence numbers, corrupted escapes, bad checksums, restarts in the middle of an operation). Its Knobs struct has one switch for each reading of an ambiguity ( Ambiguities ), so each decision is shown to work and to fail when the hub reads the other way. The tests build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DBNO08X_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_session.cpp Start-up on every transport, the state machine, restarts and recovery tests/test_i2c.cpp , test_spi.cpp The synchronous transports: H_INTN gating, WAKE, header-then-rest reads, padding tests/test_uart_shtp.cpp , test_rvc.cpp Framing, escapes, BSQ and BSN tokens, the 100 us gap, the RVC frames and their checksum tests/test_shtp_frames.cpp Every framing rule V1 to V16 and its counter tests/test_sensors.cpp , test_timestamps.cpp Report layouts and Q points, batching, timestamps and wrap-around tests/test_commands.cpp , test_control.cpp , test_frs.cpp Commands, calibration, tare, FRS read and write tests/test_variants.cpp , test_conformance.cpp The chip differences and the conformance cases of the ambiguities tests/test_errors.cpp The base Error values are 0 to 9; every chip-specific value is returned by some call; invalid input tests/test_units.cpp , test_version.cpp , test_kconfig.cpp Unit helpers and the Euler conversion, the version getters, KconfigDefaults() tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a class that is not a port, a missing hook, a hook without noexcept or with a narrowed parameter, a wrong optional hook, a Limits that is too small tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( bno08x_fuzz_bno08x_corpus ), see below examples/host/ Every host example, built with the test flags and run ( bno08x_example_<name> ) tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds tests/install_consumer/ with find_package(bno08x) tests/check_doxygen.cmake Doxygen with _config/Doxyfile and warnings as errors, when doxygen is installed

docs.text: The model does not include the driver's definition headers. Its constants (report IDs, command codes, field offsets, timing) are its own, taken from the documents with their sections, so a wrong constant in the driver cannot hide behind the same wrong constant in the model. When a test fails, check the section the model names, and fix the one that is wrong. Every behaviour a bench run shows becomes a knob of the model and a test that fails on the code before the fix.
docs.title: The model stands alone

docs.text: Everything the driver reads comes from the hub over a link a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken hub controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_bno08x.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a transport, a variant and a configuration, then a script of driver calls, and on every transfer what the link does: pass it to the model, flip bits, replace it with the fuzzer's bytes or fail it. After every call it checks the driver's promises (F1 to F11) and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines and a value-initialised result (F1); an operation is accepted only in Ready (never on UART-RVC), except a stop request (switch-off, Reset() , HubSleep() ), which after Begin() is never NotInitialized and is Busy only while the queue holds at least kOpQueue - 3 stops; InvalidArgument sends nothing (F2); every accepted operation yields exactly one OpDone , never for an unknown or finished id (F3); the events between two polls never exceed the queue plus its Dropped marker, and each has a defined kind and sensor (F4, F5); the Stats counters never decrease (F6); Faulted is left only by Begin() or HardReset() (F7); Latest() and Feature() never fail for a defined sensor once ready and never read out of bounds (F8); the Euler conversion of any quaternion stays in range (F9); an FRS read never reports more words than the buffer holds (F10); everything works with a clock that starts just below the 32-bit wrap (F11); on SPI, PS0/WAKE is high at every NRST edge and until the first H_INTN after it (F12); on UART-SHTP the model may drop Buffer Status Notifications, and writes still go out (F13). # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DBNO08X_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DBNO08X_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_bno08x ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_bno08x -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_bno08x The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_bno08x , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_bno08x/ on GCC and Clang ( bno08x_fuzz_bno08x_corpus ): the seeds for every transport, and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ).

docs.text: The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, reported in the step summary Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DBNO08X_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DBNO08X_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( bno08x_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/bno08x.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published.

docs.text: Transports ¶ One class, four ways to reach the hub. The port you write names its transport; everything above it (operations, events, calibration) is identical. The strap pins PS1 and PS0 choose the transport in the chip, so the port's kTransport must match the wiring. Datasheet sections this page relies on Protocol selection (PS1, PS0): CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.2 BNO08X Connectivity, p. 9 I2C: address, clock stretching, framing: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.2.2 I2C interface, p. 12 UART-SHTP: baud rate, framing, byte gap: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.2.3 UART-SHTP interface, p. 15 SPI: mode, WAKE, H_INTN handshake: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.2.4 SPI Interface, p. 17 UART-RVC: the 19-byte frame: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.2.5 UART-RVC interface, p. 20 SHTP header, channels and cargo reads: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 1.3.1 SHTP, p. 22 SPI timing: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 6.5.2 SPI timing, p. 46 Interrupt timing: host must answer H_INTN: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 6.5.4 Interrupt timing, p. 48 UART inputs of the RVC mode: CEVA 1000-3625 1.9, 3.1.2 UART Inputs, p. 12 Header, channels and the rules of a cargo: CEVA 1000-3535 1.10, 2.2.1 SHTP Header, p. 4 Reading cargoes, continuations and interrupts: CEVA 1000-3535 1.10, 2.5 Reading Cargoes, p. 6 Synchronous protocols: I2C and SPI handshake: CEVA 1000-3535 1.10, 3 Synchronous protocols (SPI/I2C), p. 7 SHTP over UART: control characters, BSQ and BSN: CEVA 1000-3535 1.10, 4 SHTP over UART, p. 10 Command channel and the error list: CEVA 1000-3535 1.10, 5.1 Command Channel, p. 13 Channel advertisement: CEVA 1000-3535 1.10, 5.2 Channel Advertisement, p. 15 SH-2 channel usage and report lengths: CEVA 1000-3600 1.6, 2.2 SH-2 Channel Usage, p. 4 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Transport kTransport PS1 PS0 Speed Hooks you write Needs H_INTN I2C (SHTP) Transport::I2c 0 0 100 or 400 kbit/s I2cWrite , I2cRead , IntAsserted yes SPI (SHTP) Transport::Spi 1 1 up to 3 MHz SpiTransfer , SetWake , IntAsserted yes UART (SHTP) Transport::UartShtp 1 0 3 Mbit/s UartRead , UartWrite or UartWriteByte optional UART-RVC Transport::UartRvc 0 1 115200 baud UartRead no Every port also provides EnsureInitialized() and NowUs() . Porting shows each one in code. SHTP in one page ¶ Every message is a cargo with a 4-byte header: a 15-bit length (the top bit continues a cargo), a channel and a per-channel sequence number. The driver uses channel 0 (the advertisement and the error list), 1 (executable commands), 2 (SH-2 control), 3 and 4 (input reports, normal and wake-up) and 5 (the gyro-integrated rotation vector). Cargoes can be fragmented by the hub; the driver reassembles them and never fragments what it sends: a request that does not fit one write is refused with Oversize . The advertisement at start-up carries the limits; without a limit tag the driver uses its Limits sizes (A12). The framing engine is strict. Every rule it enforces has a counter in Stats (short transfers, a length of 0xFFFF, a null header, a length of 1 to 3, an oversize cargo, a bad channel, lost or orphaned continuations, wrong continuation lengths, duplicate or skipped sequence numbers, unknown or cut-short reports). Config::resync_limit violations within Config::resync_window_ms make the driver abandon the running operations with Framing , count a resynchronisation and reset the hub, instead of guessing at the bytes. I2C ¶ The hub is a slave at 0x4A (SA0 low) or 0x4B (SA0 high). The driver reads only after H_INTN went low: first the 4-byte header, then exactly the rest of the cargo as a continuation, each as a separate transaction that ends with a STOP (no repeated start). Reading without H_INTN is possible with Config::poll_without_int , which is guarded: a BNO085 stretches the clock when it has nothing to say, a BNO086 answers with a zero-length packet (A2), so the port documents its stretch timeout. Keep the bus at 400 kbit/s or less (A39). SPI ¶ Mode 3 (clock idles high, data sampled on the second edge), most significant bit first, at most 3 MHz, full duplex. H_INTN tells the host a cargo is waiting; the host then does one duplex transfer, which may be longer than the cargo (the hub pads with zeros and a null header). To write, the driver drives WAKE low if H_INTN is not already asserted, waits for H_INTN up to Config::wake_timeout_us , does the transfer and releases WAKE. PS0 is both a strap and the WAKE line, so it must be a GPIO that is high while NRST is released: the driver drives it high before every NRST pulse and releases it on every exit (operation time-out, HardReset() , resync, hub restart), DS p18. UART with SHTP ¶ Frames start and end with 0x7E ; inside a frame 0x7E and 0x7D are escaped ( 0x7D , then the byte XOR 0x20 ). The byte after the start flag is the protocol ID: 1 for SHTP data, 0 for the hub's control frames (the buffer status query, BSQ, and the buffer status notification, BSN, in which the hub says how many bytes it can take). The BSN is a token: it holds until the next host write or until the advertised UART timeout (tag 0x81) expires, and the driver sends only while it is valid and large enough. The SHTP gives no answer time for a BSQ, so a query whose BSN has not arrived after Config::uart_bsq_retry_ms is sent again ( Stats::bsq_retries ) until the operation's own limit ends it; a lost query or notification therefore costs one retry, never the link. A write that times out half-sent is closed with a flag byte and never finished later, and a reset or resync drops a frame in progress. The hub needs at least 100 microseconds between bytes it receives, so the port either sends byte by byte through UartWriteByte (the driver paces it) or declares kPortPacesUartTx = true and implements UartWrite . Both UART modes need the 32.768 kHz clock on the board: the internal oscillator is not accurate enough at these rates (A10). UART-RVC ¶ The hub streams a 19-byte frame at 100 Hz and takes no commands: 0xAA 0xAA , an index that increases by one, yaw, pitch and roll in 0.01 degree, acceleration in milli-g, the BNO086's MI and MR bytes, reserved bytes and a checksum (the low byte of the sum of bytes 2 to 17, A6). Poll() delivers each valid frame as an EventKind::Rvc event whose v holds index, yaw, pitch, roll, ax, ay, az, mi, mr, mi_mr_valid . An ASCII banner at power-up is skipped (A9); a frame with a wrong checksum is counted and the scanner slides one byte. The $MIB text inputs the manual describes (reset, intent, dynamic calibration) are refused with Unsupported unless rvc_inputs_experimental is set, because the manual's own example checksum does not match its text (A8). Next: Sensors .

docs.text: Frames start and end with 0x7E ; inside a frame 0x7E and 0x7D are escaped ( 0x7D , then the byte XOR 0x20 ). The byte after the start flag is the protocol ID: 1 for SHTP data, 0 for the hub's control frames (the buffer status query, BSQ, and the buffer status notification, BSN, in which the hub says how many bytes it can take). The BSN is a token: it holds until the next host write or until the advertised UART timeout (tag 0x81) expires, and the driver sends only while it is valid and large enough. The SHTP gives no answer time for a BSQ, so a query whose BSN has not arrived after Config::uart_bsq_retry_ms is sent again ( Stats::bsq_retries ) until the operation's own limit ends it; a lost query or notification therefore costs one retry, never the link. A write that times out half-sent is closed with a flag byte and never finished later, and a reset or resync drops a frame in progress. The hub needs at least 100 microseconds between bytes it receives, so the port either sends byte by byte through UartWriteByte (the driver paces it) or declares kPortPacesUartTx = true and implements UartWrite . Both UART modes need the 32.768 kHz clock on the board: the internal oscillator is not accurate enough at these rates (A10).
docs.title: UART with SHTP

docs.text: The hub streams a 19-byte frame at 100 Hz and takes no commands: 0xAA 0xAA , an index that increases by one, yaw, pitch and roll in 0.01 degree, acceleration in milli-g, the BNO086's MI and MR bytes, reserved bytes and a checksum (the low byte of the sum of bytes 2 to 17, A6). Poll() delivers each valid frame as an EventKind::Rvc event whose v holds index, yaw, pitch, roll, ax, ay, az, mi, mr, mi_mr_valid . An ASCII banner at power-up is skipped (A9); a frame with a wrong checksum is counted and the scanner slides one byte. The $MIB text inputs the manual describes (reset, intent, dynamic calibration) are refused with Unsupported unless rvc_inputs_experimental is set, because the manual's own example checksum does not match its text (A8). Next: Sensors .

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ What to check when a session does not start, a call fails, or the data looks wrong. Nothing here has been confirmed on a chip: the checks come from the documents and from the faults the test model injects ( Testing and CI ). Start with GetState() and GetStats() : they narrow most problems to a line of this page. Datasheet sections this page relies on Interrupt timing: host must answer H_INTN: CEVA 1000-3927 1.17, 6.5.4 Interrupt timing, p. 48 Command channel and the error list: CEVA 1000-3535 1.10, 5.1 Command Channel, p. 13 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Begin() returns InvalidArgument ¶ A Config field is out of range: call Config::Valid() on it. The usual cause is an address other than 0x4A or 0x4B , or a timeout set to zero. Begin() returns Bus ¶ The port's EnsureInitialized() returned false, or on SPI the first SetWake() failed. Check the bus bring-up, the pins and the pull-ups before anything else. The state stays WaitAdvert , then Faulted ¶ The hub never sent its advertisement within startup_timeout_ms . Check, in this order: Power and decoupling: 3.3 V on VDD and VDDIO, 100 nF on each and on CAP. The strap pins: PS1 and PS0 must match the transport you configured and stay put until the hub is up. BOOTN: it must be high at reset. A low level starts the bootloader, which speaks a different protocol. NRST: without a SetReset hook the driver cannot pulse it; either wire it to a pull-up or provide the hook. H_INTN: on I2C and SPI the driver reads only after H_INTN went low. A line that never moves means nothing is read. Make sure IntAsserted() returns true while the line is low. The start-up time: after a reset the hub needs at least 90 ms before it asserts H_INTN. Ready() never turns true although the advertisement arrived ¶ The driver also waits for the hub's reset-complete and initialise reports (A11). Set require_init_response to false if your hub does not send the second one; read Stats for early_cargo and bad_advert . Operations end with Timeout ¶ The hub did not answer within op_timeout_ms ( frs_write_timeout_ms for a write). A sensor that is not on the board (pressure, light, proximity, humidity, temperature need the optional parts on the secondary bus) never reports, and a report the chip does not implement may never answer (A20, A31). Raise the timeout only after checking H_INTN. Error::Variant ¶ The configured chip lacks the feature. Interactive calibration and the motion request exist on the BNO086 only; check Config::variant , or set strict_variant to false to let the hub decide (A3). Error::Framing , many resyncs , seq_gap or bad_cont_len ¶ The link is corrupting bytes or the hub is not following the rules the driver expects. I2C: lower the clock to 100 kbit/s; check pull-ups and wiring length. Make sure the port ends each transfer with a STOP and never uses a repeated start. SPI: mode 3, at most 3 MHz, chip select held for the whole transfer. UART-SHTP: 3 Mbit/s needs the 32.768 kHz clock source; the port must keep 100 microseconds between bytes. Without it a frame is cut and counted in bad_escape , bad_protocol_id or oversize_frame (A10). bad_cont_len with a healthy link: the hub answers a continuation differently from the specification. Set strict_cont_len to false and tell the maintainers (A14). The hub restarts again and again ¶ hub_resets rises and Reset events appear. A watchdog or a brown-out is the usual cause: check the supply and whether the host answers H_INTN in time, because the hub gives up on a host that is too slow (A38). Call Poll() at least once per tenth of the fastest report period. Events are Dropped ¶ The event queue filled. Pop events more often, raise Limits::kEventQueue , or batch ( FeatureConfig::batch_us ) and poll less often with a larger queue. The angles jump or drift ¶ Check accuracy on each sample: values below High mean the sensor is still calibrating ( Calibration ). Near a pitch of plus or minus 90 degrees yaw and roll are ill-defined by nature of Euler angles; use the quaternion. After a tare, PersistTare() keeps it; without it a restart forgets it. Sample times are late or uneven ¶ Without TakeIntTimestamp() the time of a sample is the time of the Poll() that saw H_INTN. Provide the hook (an interrupt writing NowUs() ) for exact times ( Porting ). UART-RVC shows no frames or rvc_bad_csum ¶ The baud rate is 115200 8N1 and the hub streams without being asked. A banner at start is skipped ( rvc_banner_bytes ). A wrong checksum count with good wiring means the checksum range differs from the one assumed; rvc_csum_with_mi and rvc_csum_without_mi say which one matches (A6). Next: Contract .

Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/.
